The test image shows a corn leaf with numerous small, circular, orange to cinnamon-red pustules scattered densely across the upper leaf surface. The pustules are small, round, and appear predominantly on the upper surface. This strongly suggests a rust disease — the key question is Common_Rust vs Southern_Rust.

Southern Rust: small, circular, cinnamon-red, densely packed, almost exclusively on upper surface.
Common Rust: darker reddish-brown, more elongate/oval, on both surfaces.

The pustules here are circular and orange/cinnamon, not elongate or dark brown — pointing to Southern_Rust. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference image confirms Southern_Rust: small orange/cinnamon pustules on the upper leaf surface matching the test image well. The pustules in the test image are small, circular, densely scattered, and orange-cinnamon colored — all hallmarks of Southern Rust rather than the darker, more elongate pustules of Common Rust.
